messages:
alex: Hey @acme-sre-bob — escalation from AcmePlatform: private VPC inference nodes in us-west-2 (cluster inf-prod-02) are intermittently failing TLS handshakes to model-registry.redwood.internal. Customer sees 502 / stream resets. Any quick ideas?

acme-sre-bob: Seeing it live. Started ~2023-11-14T14:12Z, repeats every few minutes. From the node: `curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.internal:443` shows TLS handshake sometimes completes, often `SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` or `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`.

alex: Can you capture a tcpdump + conntrack? Also did they change any SG/NACL this week?

acme-sre-bob: tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
14:12:17.123456 IP 10.1.5.22.49562 > 10.2.3.44.443: Flags [S], seq 0
14:12:17.123467 IP 10.2.3.44.443 > 10.1.5.22.49562: Flags [R], seq 1
```
And conntrack shows entries with short lifetimes, occasionally `ASSURED`. AWS VPC Flow Logs around same time show `REJECT` for srcport 49562 dstport 443 with rule id referencing NACL.

dmitri: tagging infra @jamie — can you dump the NACL and NAT logs? Also paste `sudo iptables -L -n -v --line-numbers` from the node.

jamie: infra here. We rolled out a NACL tightening yesterday to harden ephemeral port range. Summary: NACL outbound allowed 1024-32767; inbound allowed ephemeral 1024-32767; explicit deny * at end. NAT gateway is standard AWS. I didn't expect NAT to use ports >32767 but NAT can translate to high ports. I'll pull NAT translation logs.

acme-sre-bob: Confirmed NAT chosen source ports frequently >40000 (e.g., 49562). If NACL only allows up to 32767 the return traffic gets dropped. That matches the `RST` right after `S` in tcpdump.

rachel: SRE note: NACLs are stateless; order matters. If outbound/return path uses a port outside allowed range, return packets are dropped. TLS may then show handshake errors or EOFs. Also check if there's any TLS inspecting appliance rewriting SNI or certs — that can cause intermittent verify errors. Run `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.internal:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.internal` to confirm SNI/cert chain consistently.

acme-sre-bob: Ran openssl about 10 times, intermittent results: sometimes full chain, sometimes `no peer certificate` or `tls_construct_client_hello:unexpected eof`. Correlates with NACL deny timestamps. AWS Flow Log excerpt: `REJECT` entries with acl-id acl-0a1b2c3d rule 110 (Deny 32768-65535).

dmitri: Can you paste the NACL rules (IDs and ordering)? Order/port ranges are important. `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --network-acl-ids acl-0a1b2c3d` output (sanitized) would help.

jamie: Pasted to PM but key lines: rule 100 allow TCP 1024-32767 inbound/outbound, rule 110 deny all. NAT translations show source ports up to 61000. So mismatch is the root cause. We bumped ephemeral ceiling to 32768 accidentally while tightening.

alex: Customer asked for repro steps — sending them a short checklist: 1) From private node run `for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://model-registry.redwood.internal || true; sleep 1; done` 2) capture tcpdump `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host model-registry.redwood.internal and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap` 3) run `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.internal:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.internal` in a loop and note failures.

rachel: Short-term mitigation: widen NACL ephemeral range to 1024-65535 (or at least 1024-49151/49152-65535) for outbound and inbound return; make sure SG egress allows ephemeral 1024-65535 too. Long-term: prefer stateful SG + NAT Gateway (stateful) or use a NAT instance that preserves port mapping consistently. Also update docs to warn about NACL ceilings for customers using NAT.

acme-sre-bob: We applied NACL change: rule 100 now Allow TCP 1024-65535 inbound/outbound. After change, we ran the curl loop and openssl loops for 30 mins with no resets. Customer reports stable streaming and no TLS errors.

deploy-bot: cluster inf-prod-02 healthcheck passing at 2309997779 :rocket:

alex: Closing the escalation. We'll follow up with a short postmortem to the customer and recommend they widen NACL ephemeral ranges or rely on SGs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

rachel: Action items: 1) Update internal KB with NACL ephemeral caveat and recommended port ranges. 2) Add a check to the VPC checklist for private deployment onboarding.

acme-sre-bob: Customer happy, leaving notes in their support ticket. Thanks all.
